reference_traces.rationale: P:S-35a9fd15002f63dd5f4a reports irreversible Z-DON alkylation of Cys273 as a proxy for the substrate-bound intermediate, and P:S-d28eb539f78aaec6fae8 documents the resulting structural rearrangement.
P:S-35a9fd15002f63dd5f4a explicitly describes Z-DON as an active-site inhibitor and the captured conformation as likely representing a substrate-bound intermediate.

P:S-929a4f21123230bd214a localizes the Fab contacts and supports calcium assignments with CheckMyMetal and difference density; P:S-d28eb539f78aaec6fae8 describes the inhibitor-associated beta-sheet and calcium-site-3 changes.

P:S-d621ee7fb9c5ef6f0d2c reports retained reactivity of all 12 patient-derived mAbs to inhibitor-bound TG3 lacking C1C2, and P:S-8b20b2ff5968116df8eb identifies the tested epitope groups and conformers.
P:S-0389ccdb512ba5a557e8 states that only approximately 10% of calcium-depleted TG3 formed complex with Fab; the final paper does not provide the requested comparative binding kinetics.

P:S-929a4f21123230bd214a supports the reported calcium assignments through CheckMyMetal and map-based replacement with magnesium, while the reviewer’s requested independent experimental ion characterization is not reported in the final-paper span.

P:S-f3ffc6823a10d4048e94 explains that available TG2 structural states lack calcium or may be influenced by crystal contacts, leaving the requested comparison to a matched active TG2 state unresolved.
P:S-bc9f31cf329ea9a53519 now states that DH63-B02 binding is consistent with a catalytic-core rather than N-terminal-domain epitope and supplies the requested contextual clarification.
P:S-0d736ba1a7e3dd556330 identifies the calcium-depleted material as cleaved TG3, documents the EDTA treatment, and distinguishes this crystallized state from prior calcium-depleted analysis.
P:S-35a9fd15002f63dd5f4a reports that released C1C2 was not visible on the chromatogram and appeared not to enter the column, making the requested final-state qualification visible.

P:S-929a4f21123230bd214a places the metal-occupancy discussion in the Results and explicitly relates the absence of magnesium binding to the reported activity effect of calcium-magnesium exchange at site 3.

limiting_points.suggested_action: The mechanistic interpretation remains bounded by use of an irreversible substrate-mimicking inhibitor as a proxy for the native enzyme-substrate intermediate.
limiting_points.text: The new structural state is informative, but its biological interpretation remains limited by the use of Z-DON as a substrate-mimicking proxy rather than direct capture of a gluten-bound intermediate.

supporting_points.suggested_action: The specific advance is the patient-antibody epitope together with the inhibitor-bound TG3 structural state and its calcium-linked rearrangement.
supporting_points.text: The work provides the first reported TG3 structure with a substrate-mimicking inhibitor in the active site, alongside definition of a patient-derived antibody paratope-epitope interaction and a calcium-site-3-linked conformational rearrangement.

questions.suggested_action: A comparison using matched calcium-containing, substrate-bound TG2 and TG3 states would define which rearrangements are TG3-specific.
questions.text: Whether the inhibitor-associated beta-sheet movement and C1C2 behavior are shared with TG2 remains unresolved because the available TG2 comparison lacks a matched calcium-containing active state.

strengths.suggested_action: The structural observations support integrated interpretation of antigen recognition, substrate occupancy, and calcium-linked conformational change.
strengths.text: The structural data connect a mapped patient-derived Fab epitope with active-site inhibitor binding, beta-sheet movement, C1C2 displacement, and changes around calcium-binding site 3.

strengths.suggested_action: The retained-reactivity experiment provides direct support for the compatibility of patient antibody recognition with the inhibitor-bound, C1C2-deficient conformer.
strengths.text: The ELISA data show that patient-derived antibodies from all three epitope groups retain reactivity to inhibitor-bound TG3 lacking C1C2, linking the structural conformer to autoantibody recognition.

summary.text: This study presents four TG3-Fab crystal structures spanning zymogen, cleaved, inhibitor-bound, and calcium-depleted states. It identifies an inhibitor-associated rearrangement in which C1C2 detach from the catalytic core and shows that patient-derived TG3 antibodies retain reactivity to the inhibitor-bound conformer lacking C1C2, supporting a structural model for recognition of TG3 enzyme-substrate complexes in dermatitis herpetiformis.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantitative binding or kinetic measurements across calcium and cleavage states would distinguish reduced complex recovery from altered Fab affinity.
weaknesses.text: The calcium-depleted preparation yielded only approximately 10% Fab-TG3 complex, but comparative binding kinetics across conformations were not reported; the basis of the low recovery therefore remains unresolved.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Independent experimental characterization of ion occupancy would complement the crystallographic and validation-server assignments.
weaknesses.text: The calcium assignments are supported by electron-density-based modeling, magnesium replacement, and CheckMyMetal analysis, but the requested independent experimental confirmation of ion identity is not part of the reported evidence.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The epitope-location context was added to the final paper.
The final paper identifies the calcium-depleted material as cleaved TG3 and describes the crystallized calcium-depleted state.
The final paper states that released C1C2 was not visible in the chromatogram and appeared not to enter the column.
The metal-occupancy discussion and calcium-magnesium exchange context are present in the final Results text.
